# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 72 (Bu-Vb Sk72)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk72
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 72
**Title (English, from literature):** Walking next to the path

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Uppathenagamana-sikk设定apadā* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 72) is a training rule from the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating the etiquette of monks while teaching the Dhamma [SuttaCentral]. Formulated as part of the *sekhiya* (training) code of the Pātimokkha, the rule states that a monastic should not teach the Dhamma while walking off or beside the path to someone who is walking on the path and is not ill (*na uppathena gacchanto pathena gacchantassa agilānassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā*) [SuttaCentral; Andrews et al. 2017]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying Vibhaṅga exposition is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Comparative vinaya literature demonstrates that this training rule is widely shared across early Buddhist monastic lineages [SuttaCentral]. Parallels are preserved across the surviving Prātimokṣa and Vinaya texts of various schools, including the Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda (*Śaikha* 62: *na utpathena gacchanto pathena gacchantasya...*), the Dharmaguptaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan, alongside the corresponding Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Parivāra counterparts [SuttaCentral; Andrews et al. 2017]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 77 internal matching segments with 30 other texts, demonstrating significant shared formulaic phrasing with adjacent *sekhiya* training rules on decorum in teaching Dhamma, notably Sekhiya 62, 63, 64, 66, 67, and 71 [DharmaNexus].
